article.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 老鼠会把社交机器人当成伙伴吗
article.context: 研究人员让真实老鼠与社交型、非社交型机器人共同生活，发现老鼠更愿意帮助曾与自己互动的社交机器人，说明简单的行为线索也足以触发社会性回应。
rows: Rats and other animals need to be highly attuned to social signals from others so they can identify friends to cooperate with and enemies to avoid.
老鼠和其他动物需要对同类发出的社会信号高度敏锐，才能识别可以合作的朋友和应当避开的敌人。
explain
To find out if this extends to non-living beings, Laleh Quinn at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues tested whether rats can detect social signals from robotic rats.
为了弄清这种能力是否也会延伸到非生命体，加州大学圣迭戈分校的拉莱·奎因及其同事测试了老鼠能否识别机器鼠发出的社会信号。
report
They housed eight adult rats with two types of robotic rat—one social and one asocial—for four days.
他们让八只成年老鼠与两种机器鼠共同生活了四天：一种具有社交行为，另一种则没有。
sequence
The robot rats were quite minimalist, resembling a chunkier version of a computer mouse with wheels to move around and colourful markings.
这些机器鼠的设计相当极简，看起来像更厚实的电脑鼠标，装有轮子可以移动，并带有彩色标记。
explain
During the experiment, the social robot rat followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors to let trapped rats escape.
实验期间，社交型机器鼠会跟随真实老鼠活动，和它们玩同样的玩具，还会打开笼门放出被困的老鼠。
sequence
Meanwhile, the asocial robot simply moved forwards and backwards and side to side.
与此同时，非社交型机器鼠只会前后、左右移动。
contrast
Next, the researchers trapped the robots in cages and gave the rats the opportunity to release them by pressing a lever.
接着，研究人员把机器鼠关进笼子，并让真实老鼠有机会通过按下杠杆将它们放出。
sequence
Across 18 trials each, the living rats were 52 per cent more likely on average to set the social robot free than the asocial one.
在每种条件各18次试验中，真实老鼠释放社交型机器鼠的平均可能性比释放非社交型机器鼠高52%。
statistic
This suggests that the rats perceived the social robot as a genuine social being.
这表明，老鼠把社交型机器鼠视为真正的社会性存在。
conclude
They may have bonded more with the social robot because it displayed behaviors like communal exploring and playing.
它们可能与社交型机器鼠建立了更强的联系，因为后者表现出了共同探索、一起玩耍等行为。
explain
This could lead to the rats better remembering having freed it earlier, and wanting the robot to return the favour when they get trapped, says Quinn.
奎因说，这可能使老鼠更清楚地记得自己先前曾救过它，并期待自己被困时机器鼠也能回报这一帮助。
explain_quote

“Rats have been shown to engage in multiple forms of reciprocal help and cooperation, including what is referred to as direct reciprocity—where a rat will help another rat that has previously helped them,” says Quinn.
奎因说：“研究已经证明，老鼠会进行多种形式的互惠帮助与合作，其中包括所谓的直接互惠——一只老鼠会帮助此前帮助过自己的另一只老鼠。”
dialogue
The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design.
考虑到机器鼠设计如此简单，真实老鼠竟如此愿意与社交型机器鼠建立关系，令人意外。
contrast
The robot was the same size as a regular rat but resembled a simple plastic box on wheels.
这台机器人与普通老鼠大小相当，却只是一个装着轮子的简单塑料盒。
explain

“We'd assumed we'd have to give it a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it to make it smell like a real rat, but that wasn't necessary,” says Janet Wiles at the University of Queensland in Australia, who helped with the research.
参与研究的澳大利亚昆士兰大学珍妮特·怀尔斯说：“我们原以为必须给它装上会动的头和尾巴、面部特征，还要加上气味，让它闻起来像真老鼠，但事实证明没有必要。”
dialogue
The finding shows how sensitive rats are to social cues, even when they come from basic robots.
这一发现表明，老鼠对社会性线索十分敏感，即便这些线索来自最简单的机器人。
conclude
Similarly, children tend to treat robots as if they are fellow beings, even when they display only simple social signals.
类似地，即使机器人只表现出简单的社会信号，儿童也往往会把它们当作同伴来对待。
compare
“We humans seem to be fascinated by robots, and it turns out other animals are too,” says Wiles.
怀尔斯说：“我们人类似乎会被机器人吸引，而事实证明，其他动物也是如此。”
dialogue
